author: Ian Young
title: "This is some good news": Indiana recorded as cheapest gas in the country - NewsBreak
text:
By Ian Young De’Onta Bush ,
1 hours ago
EVANSVILLE, Ind. (WEHT) — Indiana Governor Mike Braun says he is saving Indiana drivers some money at the pump.
On Wednesday afternoon, he announced that the gas tax suspension will be extended. In his announcement, he also boasted the state has the cheapest gas prices in the country.
“Indiana has the cheapest gas in the country because we are using every tool in the toolbox to save Hoosier families money,” says Braun. “Affordability is my number one priority.”
However, even with the gas tax suspension, some drivers are saying they are still shocked at gas prices.
‘Affordability is my number one priority’: Braun suspends Indiana sales, excise gas tax “We haven’t seen gas prices like this since COVID, so it’s pretty shocking that we have to just go through this all again, for we don’t know how long it’s going to last,” says Illinois resident Makenna Curtis.
According to AAA Fuel Prices , Indiana is currently the cheapest place in the country to get gas. Braun says he’s building on those savings by extending the gas tax suspension which saves drivers an average of 62 cents per gallon.
“I’m feeling pretty, pretty excited about it because it’s been pretty high lately,” says Indiana resident Kaylee App. “So, this is some good news. Honestly. Made my day”
“I’m not a big fan of Governor Braun, so I’m glad to see he’s doing one thing right,” says Indiana resident Debra Forrest. “I mean, the number one issue for everyone issues for people is their groceries and their gas, so if you can do anything to reduce those prices, you are doing a good job.”
Indiana leads the nation with an average gas price of $3.58 per gallon. In Kentucky, the average is $4.29 while in Illinois it’s $4.69 cents.
Kentucky’s gas tax cut: Lawmakers call it political move Drivers who commute from Illinois into Indiana say they’re tired of the rising costs.
“If I fill up in Illinois, it’s probably like $60 to $70,” says Illinois resident Makenna Curtis. “Here it’s like $50, $45 to $50. So, it’s a lot cheaper. I think it’s absurd, and I think that our governor needs to do something about it.”
Some Indiana DoorDash drivers say they’ve been driving into Kentucky for cheaper gas but now say they can finally breathe a little easier at the pump.
“I was actually in there a couple days ago, and I noticed that the prices were kind of high, and I was really surprised about that,” says Indiana resident Laura Ward. “It’s nice to be able to stay home and get gas. Whenever we would have people with tips and stuff like that, it was good tips, but you almost had to average out to make sure that it was at least a dollar per meal, because you’re paying, you know, $4.50 for gas, $4.60 for gas. So, while that it’s a little bit lower, I can be a little more lenient on what I do.”
Braun says the tax suspension extension will continue until July 7.
